summary: Document client keepalive as being potentially dangerous
description: Client-side keepalive configuration in gRPC is error-prone when client and server settings disagree. Any mismatch between client keepalive ping frequency and server enforcement policies causes RPCs to fail at unpredictable intervals with code=Unknown desc=transport is closing (TOO_MANY_PINGS / GOAWAY). In large organizations where client configurations are copy-pasted without matching server settings, connections pass light testing but drop unpredictably in production. Furthermore, changing keepalive settings requires strict deployment ordering: server configuration must be deployed everywhere before clients when enabling or tightening keepalive, and clients must be deployed before servers when disabling or relaxing it.
error_signature: code=Unknown desc=transport is closing; ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM / too_many_pings; chttp2_transport GOAWAY
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Configure a gRPC client with an aggressive keepalive time (e.g., 10s timeout) while leaving the server at the default 5-minute interval. 2. Run slow unary RPCs or active streaming RPCs. 3. Observe the server closing connections with transport is closing after ping strikes accumulate.
root_cause: Server HTTP/2 ping strike enforcement (GRPC_ARG_HTTP2_MIN_RECV_PING_INTERVAL_WITHOUT_DATA_MS and max_pings_without_data) terminates transports when clients send pings more frequently than the server permits. Additionally, C-core historically limited GRPC_ARG_HTTP2_MAX_PINGS_WITHOUT_DATA to 2 by default.
workaround_or_fix: Merged PR #25730 updating doc/keepalive.md to warn about client keepalive risks and deployment ordering. Prefer server-side keepalives or ensure server enforcement settings match client keepalive intervals prior to rolling out client changes.

summary: Keepalive watchdog timeout on slow connections
description: When a C# client (Grpc.Core 2.29.0) communicates with a Go gRPC server (1.29.1) over a slow connection (throttled to 5 KB/s) with aggressive keepalive parameters (grpc.keepalive_time_ms=3000 or 10000, grpc.keepalive_timeout_ms=3000 or 10000, grpc.keepalive_permit_without_calls=1, grpc.http2.max_pings_without_data=0), returning a 100 KB payload causes the client to abort the connection with a 'keepalive watchdog timeout' error even though the client is actively receiving data frames from the server.
error_signature: keepalive watchdog timeout; chttp2_transport.cc:2573 grpc_timer_cancel(&t->keepalive_ping_timer)
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Configure C# client ChannelOptions with grpc.keepalive_time_ms=3000 and grpc.keepalive_timeout_ms=3000. 2. Have Go server return a 100 KB random string in SayHello. 3. Limit server network bandwidth to 5 KB/s using NetLimiter 4. 4. Call SayHelloAsync in a loop; after several calls, the client fails with keepalive watchdog timeout.
root_cause: In gRPC C Core (src/core/ext/transport/chttp2/transport/chttp2_transport.cc), receiving bytes resets the keepalive_ping_timer (delaying the next ping), but if a keepalive ping has already been sent out before data reception finishes, receiving regular data bytes does NOT cancel or reset the active keepalive watchdog timer. The transport still requires the HTTP/2 PING ACK frame within GRPC_ARG_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS, which gets delayed behind large data frames on congested links.
workaround_or_fix: Closed as Working as Intended. Increase grpc.keepalive_timeout_ms (GRPC_ARG_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS) on slow or congested links so HTTP/2 PING ACK frames have sufficient time to arrive when queued behind large payload transfers.

comments.author: jtattermusch
comments.body: If a keepalive ping fails to be delivered on time, the connection is terminated as configured. You either set tight keepalive timeouts to detect broken connections quickly or set a more lenient timeout to avoid false positives on slow networks.

comments.author: yashykt

summary: Do HTTP keepalive pings work for synchronous server and client application?
description: In a C++ v1.19.1 application using synchronous client and synchronous server where the client streams data and the server mostly listens, configuring aggressive keepalive settings (GRPC_ARG_KEEPALIVE_TIME_MS=10000, GRPC_ARG_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS=2000, GRPC_ARG_KEEPALIVE_PERMIT_WITHOUT_CALLS=1) causes the client connection to drop every 10 minutes with 'chttp2_transport.cc:2765 Keepalive watchdog fired. Closing transport.' Each reconnect leaks 2 file descriptors (eventfd and eventpoll inodes), eventually exhausting the 1024 FD limit and crashing the process.
error_signature: chttp2_transport.cc:2765] Keepalive watchdog fired. Closing transport; eventfd and eventpoll inode / file descriptor exhaustion (max 1024 FDs)
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Build synchronous C++ client and synchronous C++ server on gRPC v1.19.1 (Linux epollex). 2. Set GRPC_ARG_KEEPALIVE_TIME_MS=10000 and GRPC_ARG_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 on both ends. 3. Keep streaming connection open with mostly idle reads; observe transport closing every 10 minutes and eventfd/eventpoll inode count growing by 2 per reconnect.
root_cause: In synchronous gRPC C++ applications, gRPC Core may not have active polling threads available to process keepalive pings immediately when no active read/write calls are polling the completion queue. It falls back to background threads that poll roughly every 5 seconds. Because GRPC_ARG_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS was set to 2000 ms (less than the 5-second background polling interval), the keepalive watchdog timer consistently fires before the background thread processes the PING ACK.
workaround_or_fix: Migrate from the synchronous C++ API to the asynchronous C++ API so completion queues are actively polled, or increase GRPC_ARG_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS well above the 5-second background thread polling interval (e.g., 60000 ms) and upgrade gRPC past v1.19.1.

comments.author: yashykt
comments.body: I highly recommend moving to the async API. In sync mode, when gRPC Core does not have active threads polling, you wait on background threads that poll every ~5 seconds. With a keepalive timeout of 2 seconds, the watchdog triggers before the background thread processes the ping. Increasing the timeout to a minute may work, but async API is preferred.

description: In a .NET Framework client using Grpc.Core 1.4.1, when the gRPC channel remains idle for a period of time, the very first BlockingUnaryCall fails with Grpc.Core.RpcException: Status(StatusCode=Unavailable, Detail="Endpoint read failed"), while subsequent RPC calls succeed normally because the channel reconnects after the failed attempt.
error_signature: Grpc.Core.RpcException: Status(StatusCode=Unavailable, Detail="Endpoint read failed") at Grpc.Core.Internal.AsyncCall`2.UnaryCall
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Establish a gRPC channel using Grpc.Core 1.4.1 on .NET Framework and make an initial RPC call. 2. Leave the channel completely idle until an intermediate firewall/NAT or server closes the idle TCP connection. 3. Invoke BlockingUnaryCall; observe that the first call throws StatusCode=Unavailable, Detail="Endpoint read failed" and the next call succeeds.
root_cause: When an idle connection is silently dropped by a peer, firewall, or load balancer without notifying the client, the client only detects the closed socket when attempting to read/write on the next RPC, failing that in-flight RPC with Unavailable ('Endpoint read failed') before reconnecting.
workaround_or_fix: Upgrade Grpc.Core to 1.12.0+, enable client-side keepalive pings to prevent idle connection drops or detect dead connections before an RPC is issued, and configure retry logic for transient StatusCode.Unavailable errors.

summary: Http statusCode is not translated to proper gRPC statusCode when content type is not `application/grpc`
description: After upgrading grpcio from 1.48.1 to 1.56.2 / 1.57.0, when an upstream proxy (such as Envoy during Kubernetes pod rollouts at ~50 RPS) returns an HTTP 503 Unavailable response whose Content-Type header is not 'application/grpc' (e.g., text/plain or text/html), gRPC Core logs 'hpack_parser.cc:993 Error parsing content-type metadata: invalid value' and fails the RPC with StatusCode.UNKNOWN (details='Stream removed', grpc_status:2) instead of translating HTTP 503 into StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE (grpc_status:14). Because the error is surfaced as UNKNOWN rather than UNAVAILABLE, gRPC client retry policies and subchannel reconnection logic are not triggered.

summary: grpc servers hanging with a "connection attempt timed out before receiving SETTINGS frame" error
description: Python gRPC servers and clients on grpcio 1.60.x - 1.62.1 (Python 3.11) intermittently hang/deadlock. The server process remains alive, but all incoming client connections time out after ~20 seconds with StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE: 'failed to connect to all addresses; last error: UNKNOWN: ipv4:<redacted>: connection attempt timed out before receiving SETTINGS frame' (grpc_status:14). Profiling with py-spy reveals all worker threads are frozen waiting on a Python threading lock/GIL in grpc/_channel.py (line 959) when a server handler thread simultaneously opens a client channel or performs network I/O.
error_signature: StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE details = "failed to connect to all addresses; last error: UNKNOWN: ipv4:<redacted>: connection attempt timed out before receiving SETTINGS frame" (grpc_status:14)
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Run a Python gRPC server (e.g., Dagster server or Apache Beam Dataflow worker) with grpcio 1.62.1 and Python 3.11 where worker threads also initialize gRPC client channels. 2. Observe server threads deadlocking on threading lock/GIL in grpc/_channel.py#L959. 3. Subsequent client RPCs fail after 20s with 'connection attempt timed out before receiving SETTINGS frame'.
root_cause: A threading/GIL deadlock regression in grpcio 1.60.0 - 1.62.1 (also tracked in googleapis/python-bigtable#949) causes native/Python channel threads to stall indefinitely, preventing the server from completing the HTTP/2 handshake (sending the initial SETTINGS frame) on new connections.
workaround_or_fix: Fixed and backported in grpcio v1.62.2 (and v1.63.0+). Workarounds for older setups: upgrade grpcio to >= 1.62.2, downgrade grpcio to <= 1.58.0, or downgrade google-api-core to <= 2.16.2. Also ensure old gRPC server processes are cleanly terminated so zombie processes do not hold the listening port.

summary: grpc-status UNKNOWN instead of UNAUTHENTICATED when server responds with 401 but content-type is not application/grpc
description: When calling a gRPC service protected by Google Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) without valid credentials using grpcio >= 1.62.0, IAP responds with HTTP `:status: 401`, `content-type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`, `x-goog-iap-generated-response: true`, and `grpc-status: 16` (UNAUTHENTICATED). Although hpack_parser.cc initially maps HTTP 401 to `grpc-status: 16`, when the 36-byte HTML body arrives in a DATA frame with END_STREAM, `chttp2_transport.cc:2084` attempts to parse it as a gRPC length-prefixed frame, fails with `Deframe data frame: UNKNOWN: Bad GRPC frame type 0x49`, and overwrites the final call status to `StatusCode.UNKNOWN` (`details = "Stream removed"`, `grpc_status: 2`).

summary: Async write() on unimplemented stream-stream RPC fails with INTERNAL "execute_batch" error half of the time
description: When using Python's `grpc.aio` asynchronous client to invoke a bidirectional (stream-stream) RPC against a server in a separate process that does not implement the service (e.g., calling `ServerReflectionStub.ServerReflectionInfo()` followed by `await rpc.write(...)`), roughly 46% of calls fail with `AioRpcError: StatusCode.INTERNAL, details = "Internal error from Core", debug_error_string = 'Failed "execute_batch": (<grpc._cython.cygrpc.SendMessageOperation object>,)'` instead of returning `StatusCode.UNIMPLEMENTED`.
error_signature: AioRpcError: status = StatusCode.INTERNAL, details = "Internal error from Core", debug_error_string = "Failed \"execute_batch\": (<grpc._cython.cygrpc.SendMessageOperation object>,)"; error=UNKNOWN:Attempt to send message after stream was closed
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Start a gRPC Python server in a separate process without registering ServerReflection. 2. Using grpc.aio.insecure_channel, call stub.ServerReflectionInfo() and immediately await rpc.write(ServerReflectionRequest()) in a loop of 100 iterations. 3. Observe ~46 out of 100 calls raising StatusCode.INTERNAL ('Failed execute_batch: SendMessageOperation') instead of StatusCode.UNIMPLEMENTED.
root_cause: Race condition in `grpc.aio` stream-stream calls: `await rpc.write()` schedules a `SendMessageOperation` batch asynchronously. If the server immediately closes the stream with `UNIMPLEMENTED` before the scheduled write batch executes in C Core, Core rejects the batch with `error=UNKNOWN:Attempt to send message after stream was closed`, which Cython (`cygrpc`) surfaces as `StatusCode.INTERNAL: Failed "execute_batch"` rather than the server's trailing status (`UNIMPLEMENTED`).
workaround_or_fix: Wait for initial metadata (`await rpc.wait_for_connection()` or check stream state) before issuing `rpc.write()`, or treat `StatusCode.INTERNAL` with `SendMessageOperation` execute_batch failure on closed streams as a stream-closed race in `grpc.aio`.

summary: DNS lookup causes large delay (> 20s) if AAAA query never returns
description: When connecting to a host whose DNS server responds to IPv4 `A` queries immediately but silently drops or never responds to IPv6 `AAAA` queries, gRPC's default `c-ares` DNS resolver stalls for over 20 seconds before completing name resolution. Switching to `GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER=native` reduces total execution time from >20 seconds to 1-2 seconds.
error_signature: 20+ second latency during DNS name resolution in src/core/lib/event_engine/ares_resolver.cc and src/core/ext/filters/client_channel/resolver/dns/c_ares/grpc_ares_wrapper.cc when AAAA query times out
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Connect a gRPC client (e.g., grpcio 1.60.0) to a domain whose DNS server answers A record queries but never responds to AAAA queries. 2. Run with GRPC_TRACE=cares_resolver,dns_resolver GRPC_VERBOSITY=DEBUG. 3. Observe >20s delay waiting for the AAAA query to time out in c-ares before the channel connects using the already-received A record.
root_cause: gRPC Core (`grpc_ares_wrapper.cc` and `ares_resolver.cc`) issues two separate `ares_gethostbyname` calls—one for `AF_INET` (`A`) and one for `AF_INET6` (`AAAA`)—and waits for BOTH queries to finish or time out before returning resolved addresses to the channel. In contrast, `ares_getaddrinfo` with `AF_UNSPEC` (implemented in `c-ares#551`) sends both queries and stops retrying as soon as at least one address family succeeds.
workaround_or_fix: Set `GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER=native` in the environment, or configure a shorter c-ares query timeout via the channel argument `GRPC_ARG_DNS_ARES_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS` (`grpc.dns_ares_query_timeout_ms`). Long-term fix is migrating gRPC Core from `ares_gethostbyname` to `ares_getaddrinfo` with `AF_UNSPEC`.

summary: gRPC call fails when DNS re-resolving involved after Kubernetes service IP change
description: In an AKS cluster, Service A (C# Grpc.Core 2.43.0) makes a successful RPC to Service B, and then the channel goes IDLE. Service B is redeployed and gets a new Kubernetes IP (changing from `10.0.237.89` to `10.0.94.157`). When Service A makes the next RPC, `pick_first` exits IDLE and attempts to connect to the cached obsolete IP `10.0.237.89:443`. After a 20-second TCP `connect() timed out`, `pick_first` transitions to `TRANSIENT_FAILURE`, triggers c-ares DNS re-resolution (which finds the new IP `10.0.94.157`), and simultaneously fails the queued RPC with `StatusCode="Unavailable", Detail="failed to connect to all addresses"` (`Failed to pick subchannel`) instead of waiting for the newly resolved IP.
error_signature: Grpc.Core.RpcException: Status(StatusCode="Unavailable", Detail="failed to connect to all addresses", DebugException="Failed to pick subchannel" at client_channel.cc:3135 / tcp_client_posix.cc:114 connect() timed out)
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Make an RPC from Service A to Service B over a DNS target URI using default pick_first policy, then let the channel enter IDLE. 2. Redeploy Service B so its DNS A record points to a new IP and the old IP blackholes TCP SYNs. 3. Invoke a new RPC with WaitForReady=false (default). 4. Observe a 20s TCP connect timeout to the old IP followed by immediate StatusCode.Unavailable ('failed to connect to all addresses') at the exact moment DNS re-resolution is triggered.
root_cause: By design in gRPC's `pick_first` LB policy, DNS re-resolution is only triggered when the existing subchannel list fails to connect and enters `TRANSIENT_FAILURE`. For RPCs with `WaitForReady=false` (the default), any RPC queued waiting for a subchannel pick is immediately failed as soon as the channel transitions from `CONNECTING` to `TRANSIENT_FAILURE` (`client_channel.cc:3125 LB pick failed`), before the asynchronous DNS re-resolution completes.
workaround_or_fix: Enable gRPC Retries in the channel's ServiceConfig for `StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE` (or set `WaitForReady=true` on the CallOptions) so the RPC automatically retries or waits across the `TRANSIENT_FAILURE` transition while DNS re-resolution connects to the new IP.

summary: grpc raises StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE while invoking a service twice with recreated channel
description: When invoking the same gRPC service twice in Python by creating or garbage-collecting a channel inside a helper function without keeping the channel reference alive or reusing it, the second RPC invocation fails with `_Rendezvous of RPC that terminated with (StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE, ...)` because the underlying channel or subchannel is prematurely shut down or disconnected.
error_signature: _Rendezvous of RPC that terminated with (StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE, {"description":"OS Error / Socket closed"})
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Create a gRPC channel and stub inside a short-lived scope or close/recreate channels rapidly between back-to-back unary calls. 2. Invoke the same service method a second time and observe _Rendezvous StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE.
root_cause: Creating and destroying gRPC channels per request or allowing the `grpc.Channel` object to be garbage-collected while stubs/calls are still active causes premature channel termination.
workaround_or_fix: Reuse a long-lived `grpc.Channel` instance across RPC calls (or use `with grpc.insecure_channel(...) as channel:` context managers introduced in newer grpcio releases) rather than recreating channels per RPC.

comments.author: nathanielmanistaatgoogle
comments.body: Ensure the grpc.Channel object is kept alive for the lifetime of the stub and reused across RPC invocations.

summary: _InactiveRpcError of RPC that terminated with StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE: "failed to connect to all addresses"
description: Python gRPC client fails to connect to a target device endpoint, raising `grpc._channel._InactiveRpcError: <_InactiveRpcError of RPC that terminated with: status = StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE, details = "failed to connect to all addresses">` when the target host/port is unreachable, listening only on localhost (`127.0.0.1`), or blocked by firewall rules.
error_signature: grpc._channel._InactiveRpcError: status = StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE details = "failed to connect to all addresses" (grpc_status:14)
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Start a gRPC server bound to localhost or an unreachable port/interface. 2. Connect from a remote Python gRPC client and invoke a unary RPC. 3. Observe _InactiveRpcError with StatusCode.UNAVAILABLE: failed to connect to all addresses.
root_cause: The client subchannel failed TCP/TLS connection establishment to every resolved IP address for the target URI (e.g., server not running, bound to `127.0.0.1` instead of `0.0.0.0` / `[::]`, or blocked by firewall/proxy).
workaround_or_fix: Verify the gRPC server binds to `0.0.0.0:<port>` or `[::]:<port>`, verify network connectivity and proxy settings (`http_proxy` / `no_proxy`), and enable `GRPC_VERBOSITY=debug GRPC_TRACE=tcp,http` to inspect the underlying socket error.

comments.author: gnossen
comments.body: 'failed to connect to all addresses' indicates the client could not establish a TCP connection to any resolved address. Check server binding address, firewall rules, and HTTP proxy environment variables.

summary: Handle grpc.RpcError exceptions specially in request iterators
description: In Python gRPC streaming RPCs, when a client-supplied request iterator raises an exception (including another `grpc.RpcError` from an upstream gRPC call), gRPC Python catches the exception in the request consumption thread, logs it, and terminates the outer RPC with a generic `StatusCode.UNKNOWN` (`details = "Exception iterating requests!"`) without preserving the original exception details or status code.
error_signature: StatusCode.UNKNOWN: "Exception iterating requests!" when an exception or nested grpc.RpcError is raised inside a streaming request generator
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Pass a generator function as the request_iterator to a client-streaming or stream-stream RPC in Python. 2. Raise an exception or let an upstream grpc.RpcError propagate inside the generator. 3. Observe the outer RPC failing with StatusCode.UNKNOWN ('Exception iterating requests!') without the inner RpcError status or message.
root_cause: The request iterator consumer thread in `grpc._channel` catches all `Exception` instances uniformly and aborts the call with `StatusCode.UNKNOWN` and static text `"Exception iterating requests!"`.
workaround_or_fix: Catch exceptions inside the request iterator before yielding, log or record the causal error context on the client side, and explicitly cancel the RPC or propagate structured metadata.

comments.author: nathanielmanistaatgoogle
comments.body: When a request iterator raises an exception, the client cannot send arbitrary status codes to the server (only cancellation), though preserving local error cause information on the resulting client-side RpcError is useful.

summary: grpc doesn't work with a message ("Channel closed!") - StatusCode.CANCELLED
description: Python gRPC client calls fail immediately with `<_Rendezvous of RPC that terminated with: status = StatusCode.CANCELLED, details = "Channel closed!">` when a stub method is invoked after the `with grpc.insecure_channel(...) as channel:` block has exited or after `channel.close()` has been called.
error_signature: _Rendezvous of RPC that terminated with: status = StatusCode.CANCELLED details = "Channel closed!"
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Create a stub inside a `with grpc.insecure_channel('localhost:50051') as channel:` context manager block and return the stub from a helper function. 2. Call a method on the returned stub outside the `with` block. 3. Observe StatusCode.CANCELLED with details = 'Channel closed!'.
root_cause: Exiting the `with grpc.insecure_channel(...) as channel:` context manager automatically invokes `channel.close()`, which cancels all active RPCs and rejects any subsequent RPC invocations on stubs bound to that channel with `StatusCode.CANCELLED: Channel closed!`.
workaround_or_fix: Keep the `with grpc.insecure_channel(...) as channel:` block active for the entire duration of all stub calls, or manage the `channel` lifecycle explicitly and only call `channel.close()` during application shutdown.

comments.author: gnossen
comments.body: Using `with grpc.insecure_channel(...) as channel:` closes the channel as soon as the `with` block exits. Do not return a stub created inside a `with` block for later use; keep the channel open until you are done making RPCs.

summary: Role and configuration of GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER environment variable in gRPC DNS resolution (grpc dns解析中的GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER这个参数的作用是什么)
description: Clarification and documentation on how the `GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER` environment variable controls which DNS resolver implementation gRPC C Core uses (`ares` vs. `native`), when `c-ares` is selected by default, and how fallback behavior works across platforms and service config / SRV lookups.
error_signature: GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER=ares vs GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER=native; dns_resolver_ares.cc / dns_resolver_connectivity
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Inspect gRPC DNS resolver selection by setting GRPC_VERBOSITY=DEBUG GRPC_TRACE=dns_resolver. 2. Compare behavior between default (GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER=ares) and OS native resolver (GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER=native).
root_cause: By default, gRPC C Core uses `ares` (`c-ares` library) if gRPC was built with `c-ares` support because `c-ares` supports asynchronous non-blocking queries, DNS SRV record lookups (required for `grpclb`), and TXT record lookups (for DNS service configs). However, `c-ares` bypasses the OS NSS / systemd-resolved / macOS `scutil` resolver stack, which can fail in complex VPN, `/etc/nsswitch.conf`, or split-DNS setups.
workaround_or_fix: Set `GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER=native` to force gRPC to use the OS standard `getaddrinfo()` resolver when `c-ares` fails in VPN/container environments (noting that `native` does not support DNS SRV or TXT service config lookups).

comments.author: apolcyn
comments.body: The default is `ares` if gRPC is built with c-ares support. Available values for GRPC_DNS_RESOLVER are `ares` (default, supports SRV and TXT lookups asynchronously) and `native` (uses OS getaddrinfo()).
